task.description:
Implement REQ-373 per the validated design at lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md (PASSED design gate, handoffs/WF02-REQ373-20260921/step-01c-design-gate-regate.json). Verify branch first: `git branch --show-current` MUST equal feature/WF02-REQ373-20260921 -- STOP and report FAIL if not. This is a BACKEND-ONLY change: do not touch anything under web/.

Follow WF-02 Step 2a's procedure (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md): implement lib/letflow/**/*.ex per the design; write priv/repo/migrations/*.exs per the design's DB spec; run `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (fix and retry on failure); run `mix ecto.migrate` against a real/Docker-provisioned test DB per docs/anti-patterns.md's Docker fallback if no local toolchain (verify docs/anti-patterns.md's 'No Elixir/mix toolchain' entry first -- a toolchain IS present on this host at /c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix per that entry, check before concluding otherwise); run `mix format --check-formatted` (fix formatting if it fails). Self-review checklist per WF-02 Step 2a: no string interpolation of tenant/user input into raw SQL; no unresolved {:ok, _} = match on an external-I/O-reachable path; every state transition persisted via Letflow.Repo inside the transition; new public functions have a one-line @doc; every call site of any changed function signature still compiles.

Specifically implement, per the design doc: (1) the schema decision -- status column (Ecto.Enum, values: [:ACTIVE, :RETIRED]) plus version identity directly on service_catalog, plus the new service_catalog_versions sibling archive table, with the reasoning stated in the moduledoc verbatim in substance; (2) a publish/N operation creating a new ACTIVE version, archiving the prior version's snapshot into service_catalog_versions, without touching any already-recorded INSTANCE_STARTED pin payload; (3) a retire/N operation that fails resolution for NEW resolve/4 calls outright (per the design's explicit AC4 resolution -- no fallback to current version) while leaving PinResolver.pin_for/3 unaffected (structural: pin_for/3 never queries the catalog); (4) a new module implementing PinResolver.Lookup's catalog_lookup contract backed by the versioned catalog (module_lookup remains out of scope for PLC-01 -- explicitly return :not_found or equivalent, do not build module_ref resolution); (5) wire this new Lookup into Engine.create/2's pin_lookup/2 helper in place of PinResolver.default_lookup/0 for catalog_entry references ONLY -- variable_schema/module_ref pin_lookup/2 behavior must remain byte-unchanged; (6) publish/retire HTTP routes per the design, gated by the EXISTING :AdminServicesManage permission (verify lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's existing prefix-match clause covers the new route paths -- if it doesn't automatically, you MUST NOT invent a new permission atom, adjust the route paths to match the existing policy's prefix instead, or flag this in issues for REVIEWER if genuinely unresolvable); (7) the migration exactly per the design's column/index/constraint spec.

Do NOT modify lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex's existing PIN-01..05 machinery beyond what the design explicitly calls for (the Lookup wiring at the create/2 call site) -- this is released, tested machinery per the requirement text, not something to refactor. Do NOT build PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning -- explicitly out of scope, confirm your moduledoc states this with a citation of pin_resolver.ex's own SCOPE GAP language, per the requirement's own AC7.

Write a moduledoc on every new/changed core module stating the schema decision and its reasoning (AC1), the retire-vs-fallback decision (AC4), and the PLC-01 out-of-scope citation (AC7) -- these three moduledoc statements are independently checked by SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR later, do not skip them.

Run `mix letflow.check` yourself and quote real output before completing this handoff (AC8 requires this eventually at RELEASE-VALIDATOR, but confirm it compiles/formats/passes locally first so REVIEWER isn't blocked by a trivial failure). Commit and push all new/changed files (explicit filenames, never -A) to origin feature/WF02-REQ373-20260921 before ending your turn. Complete the handoff with your genuine PASS/FAIL result and artifacts_out listing every file touched.
acceptance_criteria: all migrations apply cleanly against a fresh DB
no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user data
all callers of any changed function signature compile
publish/retire operations gated behind :AdminServicesManage, no new permission invented
PLC-01/module_ref explicitly out of scope, cited in moduledoc
moduledoc states the schema decision (AC1) and retire-vs-fallback decision (AC4) with reasoning

result.summary:
Implemented REQ-373 per the validated design (lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md), verified branch feature/WF02-REQ373-20260921 before editing. (1) Migration priv/repo/migrations/20260921000003_add_service_catalog_versioning.exs: adds version/version_id/status/published_at/retired_at to service_catalog (DB-level defaults backfill existing rows; published_at nullable-added, UPDATEd from created_at, then set NOT NULL) plus chk_service_catalog_status/chk_service_catalog_version_length CHECK constraints, and a new append-only service_catalog_versions archive table (version_id PK, unique (service_id,version) index, deliberately no FK per design §4/§9 OQ-1). Written as up/0 + down/0 (not change/0) because the backfill UPDATE isn't Ecto-auto-reversible -- matches 20260921000002_add_kind_to_tenant_role.exs's own precedent. Verified both directions against the real Docker Postgres test DB (mix ecto.migrate, mix ecto.rollback, mix ecto.migrate again) -- all clean. (2) Entry schema (lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex): five new fields (status as plain Ecto.Enum [:ACTIVE,:RETIRED], no values: remapping, per the design's casing reconciliation), publish_changeset/2 and retire_changeset/1, plus a moduledoc section stating the schema decision, AC4 retire-vs-fallback reasoning, and the PLC-01 out-of-scope citation. (3) Letflow.ServiceCatalog (lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex): publish/3 (transactional: fetch current row, reject duplicate version against current+archive, archive current row's snapshot into service_catalog_versions unconditionally, update row in place with a fresh version_id/version/status:ACTIVE/published_at/retired_at:nil) and retire/1 (not_found/already_retired/ok, status:RETIRED+retired_at, no archive insert) -- both with full @doc reasoning restating the design's publish-invariant and retire-fails-outright arguments verbatim in substance. register/1 now also stamps version_id (Ecto.UUID.generate/0) and published_at (=now) on the base struct, mirroring created_at/updated_at -- REQUIRED fix discovered during verification: Entry's field/3 declarations give version/status Elixir-level defaults ('1'/:ACTIVE) that Ecto picks up automatically, but version_id/published_at have no such default, so Ecto.Repo.insert/2 was sending explicit NULL for both (Ecto always sends every schema field's current struct value, never silently relying on a DB column default for a field the schema itself declares) -- this violated the new NOT NULL published_at constraint on every register/1 call until fixed. Full moduledoc section added stating the schema decision + reasoning (AC1), matching the design verbatim in substance. (4) New module lib/letflow/service_catalog/pin_lookup.ex (Letflow.ServiceCatalog.PinLookup): build/0 constructs a PinResolver.Lookup.t() copying module_lookup/variable_schema_lookup verbatim from PinResolver.default_lookup/0 and replacing catalog_lookup with this module's own catalog_lookup/1 (no row -> :not_found; ACTIVE row -> {:ok, %{resolved_id: version_id, version: version}}; RETIRED row -> :not_found, implementing AC4's fails-outright decision at the one place resolve/4 calls in). Moduledoc cites pin_resolver.ex's own SCOPE GAP language verbatim per AC7. (5) lib/letflow/engine.ex: pin_lookup/2's Map.get/3 default changed from PinResolver.default_lookup() to PinLookup.build() -- only that one call-site token changed; attrs[:pin_lookup] caller-override behavior, _prefix handling, and the resolve/4 call site itself are byte-unchanged. New module alias added. (6) New module lib/letflow/service_catalog/version.ex (Letflow.ServiceCatalog.Version): Ecto schema for the archive table, version_id PK (autogenerate: false -- copied verbatim from the live row), archive_changeset/1. (7) Two new routes on lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex: POST /:service_id/versions (handle_publish/2, parses version + publish_attrs() JSON body, 201/404/409/422) and POST /:service_id/retire (handle_retire/2, no body, 200/404/409) -- both declared authz_post ... :AdminServicesManage, the EXISTING permission (verified lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's endpoint_policy_key/2 prefix-match clause -- any POST/PATCH/DELETE under /admin/services -- already covers both new paths with zero authorization.ex change, exactly as the design predicted; no new permission atom invented). service_record_json/1 extended with the five new fields (version/version_id/status/published_at/retired_at, snake_case/ISO-8601, per design §9 OQ-3's ELIXIR-DEV-level naming call).

Self-review: no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user input (the one raw-SQL-adjacent migration statement is a fixed literal UPDATE, no interpolation at all); no unresolved {:ok, _} = match on any external-I/O path; publish/3's transaction persists via Repo inside the transaction, no async coupling; every new public function has a @doc; register/1's fix confirmed every existing caller (register!/1 test helpers across the suite) still passes. No file under web/ touched. lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex itself was NOT modified (only its already-existing pin_lookup/2 call site in engine.ex, as the design explicitly scoped).

Verification, real output quoted: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- 0 warnings/errors on the letflow app (deps' own pre-existing warnings, e.g. jose/eqrcode, are unrelated and unchanged). `mix format --check-formatted` -- clean (no output) after running `mix format` on every touched file. `mix letflow.check` -- first full run surfaced two real regressions from this branch (register/1's missing version_id/published_at stamping, fixed in service_catalog.ex; and two pre-existing test fixtures -- test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs's insert_entry!/1 and 5 raw-SQL INSERT statements in test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs's AC1/AC2 DB-CHECK tests -- that bypass ServiceCatalog.register/1 and construct/INSERT service_catalog rows directly, now needing the two new required fields stamped/listed explicitly; fixed both, mechanical, no test-design content changed) plus a large, separately-diagnosed batch of ~41 unrelated failures traced via docs/anti-patterns.md's own documented 'Stale tenant_template schema surviving a migration-adding commit' entry to 17 stale letflow_test* databases left over from an earlier session on this shared Docker Postgres container (versions_missing=[20260921000002], a pre-existing migration from ISS-0774, unrelated to this branch) -- dropped all 17 stale DBs per that entry's documented fix, re-ran clean. Final full run: `Result: 374/375 passed (2/2 properties, 372/373 tests); Failed: 1 test` -- the one remaining failure is Letflow.Docs.RequirementStatusInvariantsTest's A9 check (docs/status/requirement_status.v21.yaml declares 12 entries, 13 actually on disk), confirmed via `git log`/`git status` to be pre-existing docs bookkeeping drift from this run's own Step 00 git-setup commit (4fad7382), touching a file (docs/status/) this handoff's owned_modules does not include and this diff does not modify -- flagged in issues below rather than silently fixed, not blocking REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER since it is unrelated to lib/letflow or priv/repo/migrations.

Migration reversibility self-review: rewrote the initial change/0 draft to up/0+down/0 after discovering `mix ecto.rollback` genuinely fails on a bare execute/1 SET NOT NULL statement inside change/0 (Ecto cannot auto-reverse it) -- verified the fix by running migrate -> rollback -> migrate again against the real Docker Postgres test DB, all three clean.
issues: docs/status/requirement_status.v21.yaml's declared entries: count (12) has drifted from actual on-disk entries (13), per Letflow.Docs.RequirementStatusInvariantsTest's A9 check -- pre-existing, introduced by this run's own Step 00 git-setup commit (4fad7382), not touched by this handoff (docs/status/ is outside owned_modules). Flagged for DOC-UPDATER/REVIEWER to fix the declared count; does not block this handoff's PASS since it is unrelated to lib/letflow or priv/repo/migrations.

Design §9 OQ-1 (no FK from service_catalog_versions.service_id to service_catalog.service_id, to avoid giving delete/1 a new out-of-scope FK-violation failure mode) implemented exactly as designed -- REVIEWER should confirm this tradeoff (orphaned archive rows after a delete) remains acceptable, per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's prior pass-through of this same open question.

register/1's stamping of version_id/published_at (new in this implementation, not spelled out in that exact form in the design beyond 'four additional stamped fields') was required to make Ecto.Repo.insert/2 actually pick up sensible values -- REVIEWER should double check this reasoning (Ecto sends every schema-declared field's struct value explicitly, including NULL, never relying on a DB column default for a field the schema itself declares) against Entry's field/3 declarations.

Two pre-existing test files (test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs, test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs) were mechanically patched to stamp/list the two new required columns in their direct-construction fixtures (bypassing ServiceCatalog.register/1 by design, to test DB-level CHECK constraints and reaper behavior independently) -- no test-design content changed, purely additive column handling. TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR should confirm these mechanical edits are in scope for them to review rather than re-litigate.
